topic.title: Experiences Are The New Logo
topic.claim: Young Indians saying they'd rather spend on a wellness retreat than a branded bag aren't rejecting status spending, they're just doing status spending that doesn't photograph as a logo anymore.
topic.behaviour: Under-40 buyers account for 60% of India's luxury purchases versus 40% globally, Gen Z drives about 47% of fashion-and-lifestyle spend, and professionals still put 15-20% of income into premium products while increasingly prioritising travel and wellness over owning branded goods.
topic.mechanism: A watch or a bag used to be the visible marker of status, now the visible marker is a story, a reel from a retreat, a boarding pass, so the spend hasn't dropped, only the format of the flex has changed.
topic.group: Urban professionals in their 20s and 30s with disposable luxury spending power
real_details: India's luxury market is valued near $10.6 billion, growing toward $18.8 billion by 2034
under-40 buyers account for 60% of purchases versus 40% globally
Gen Z drives about 47% of fashion-and-lifestyle spend
professionals still allocate 15-20% of income to premium products
Bain estimates India has 20-25 million active luxury consumers, with millennials making up 40-45% of that base
topic.news_peg: Report on young Indians shifting luxury spending toward experiences, October 2026
topic.why_now: Published this month amid festive and wedding-season luxury spending

score.why: Fits her 'wellness is marketing wearing a yoga mat' belief exactly: it's still status spending, just repackaged so it doesn't photograph as a logo.
